title: Gadsby, the novel without an E
hook: A 1939 novel of about 50,000 words was written almost entirely without the letter E.
peek: In 1939 Ernest Vincent Wright published Gadsby, a full-length novel written to avoid the letter E, the most common letter in English. To manage it, he said, he tied down the E key on his typewriter.
lede: E is the most common letter in English, turning up in about one letter in eight. In 1939 Ernest Vincent Wright published Gadsby, a novel of about 50,000 words that avoids it completely. That rules out "the", "he", "she", "they" and most past tenses ending in "-ed". Writing without one letter is called a lipogram.

bullets.text: In his introduction, Wright explains that he tied down the E key of his typewriter while writing, so none could slip in by habit. He said friends had told him such a book could not be done.
The plot follows John Gadsby, a middle-aged man who rallies the young people of his sleepy town, Branton Hills, to improve it. Under their efforts the town flourishes and grows into a city.

Without E, whole families of words vanish. Of the numbers from one to ten, only two, four and six survive, and Wright had to find roundabout ways to say simple things, which gives the prose an odd feel.
The book was put out by a small vanity press and sold few copies at first. Original copies are now scarce and sought after, and Gadsby is often cited whenever people discuss constrained writing.
